O.content: The printed title reads "Selected High-Growth Quarters: Ad Spend vs Sales".
The visible chart contains five labeled blue points: Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, and Q6.
No visible legend, control-group marks, causal annotation, or full-quarter data table is shown.

B.text: If a budget approval requires full-quarter coverage or evidence that advertising caused sales changes, a scatterplot limited by its title to selected high-growth quarters and lacking causal controls is insufficient; the evidence-review option is then appropriate.
B.conditions: Applies when decision standards require representative or causal evidence beyond a selected observational sample.

O.content: The printed title reads "Selected High-Growth Quarters: Ad Spend vs Sales".
The horizontal-axis inscription reads "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)"; labeled ticks include 30, 40, 50, 60, and 70.
The vertical-axis inscription reads "Sales ($ thousands)"; labeled ticks include 60 through 170.
Blue points labeled Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, and Q6 progress from lower-left to upper-right; Q6 is right of and above Q5, and Q5 is right of and above Q4.

B.text: If the horizontal axis encodes advertising spend and the vertical axis encodes sales, as their printed labels state, then points farther right and higher represent quarters with greater plotted spend and sales. If this selected-quarter association is considered sufficient and generalizable evidence for a broader budget change, it supports approving an ad-budget increase; the chart alone does not establish causation or represent all quarters.
B.conditions: Applies only to the plotted quarters labeled Q2–Q6 and assumes the selected high-growth sample is relevant to a broader advertising-budget decision.
